project: defender — an LLM SOC-analyst agent (python, pytest, uv)

gate.test: cd defender && flock /tmp/defender-pytest.lock uv run pytest tests/ -m "not live and not gate" -n auto --dist loadfile --ignore tests/e2e/test_540_box_boundary.py
checks: the baseline-ratcheted custom lints under tooling/lint/lint_*.py (monkeypatch, unsafe-jsonl-io, raw-git-subprocess, unanchored-default, vulture, duplicate-helpers, …) — each blocks only on a NEW finding, and each documents an inline-suppression escape hatch in its own module
gate.notes: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the source of truth — run what it runs; don't trust this list to stay current. Running in a git worktree? The shared `.venv` editable install points at the main checkout — prepend `PYTHONPATH=<worktree-root>` to the pytest call or you test the wrong tree. EVERY pytest invocation on this box goes through one lock — prefix it `flock /tmp/defender-pytest.lock`, ad-hoc subsets and adversary runs included, not just the command above. Two sessions launching fleets independently put 20 xdist workers on 12 cores and OOM-killed the container; the lock makes them take the box in turn instead of thrashing it. It costs nothing when nothing else is running. `test` above is CI's full-suite command, recorded so you can read what CI runs — a spec-flow leaf never runs it; it runs its own suite's files.

tests.harness: defender/tests/e2e/_replay_harness.py — a new scenario is a few lines of `Turn(...)`, not fresh plumbing. Build on it rather than inventing parallel machinery.
tests.idioms: Fakes enter through the entry point's injection seams (a `deps` parameter, a constructor argument), never `monkeypatch.setattr` — CI ratchets new setattr sites (`tooling/lint/lint_monkeypatch.py`).

conventions.principles: docs/principles.md — the project's engineering principles (threat model, fail closed/loud/fast, no apologetic programming). Read it in full; a design doc's principles section adds to or overrides it for that issue.
conventions.dangerLens: adversarial input — alert data is attacker-influenced by definition, and malicious input is well-formed on purpose. Use this as write-tests' danger lens unless the change's danger zone is clearly elsewhere (environment/resource, or concurrency when the design admits parallel invocation).

codeGraph.notes: defender is a namespace package (no defender/__init__.py; pyproject at defender/, not the repo root), so pyrefly's import root defaults to defender/ and `defender.x` imports silently resolve to Unknown. searchPath is relative to configDir: `..` = repo root (makes `defender` a top-level package, mirroring pytest's pythonpath=['..']), `.` = defender/. The pyrefly-refs helper writes a temp configDir/pyrefly.toml from these and removes it per run.
